prayerExcerpt.en-US: How powerfully do the martyrs cry out to us by their example, exhorting us to despise a false and wicked world!
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Quão poderosamente clamam a nós os mártires pelo seu exemplo, exortando-nos a desprezar um mundo falso e perverso!

meta.face: Three clearly different men of Roman Umbria. SABINUS (centre), about sixty, after the Ravenna mosaic: a LONG, NARROW face with a SQUARE, level chin — a LOW, straight FRINGE of short grey-brown hair combed forward across the forehead (NOT bald); LARGE, wide-open, dark ALMOND eyes under straight brows; a LONG, thin nose; lean cheeks; a small, firm mouth; a SHORT, trimmed grey-brown beard following the jaw. MARCELLUS (left), about thirty-five: a BROAD, SQUARE, strong-jawed face, olive-tanned, with close black curls, heavy straight black brows, dark eyes, a short, straight nose, a firm mouth, and a close black beard. EXUPERANTIUS (right), about twenty-five: a SOFT, ROUND face with a fair olive complexion, WAVY chestnut hair to the ears, round hazel eyes under arched brows, a small, slightly upturned nose, and a short, soft first beard.
meta.basis: Sabinus's face follows his figure among the procession of martyrs in the sixth-century mosaic of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna (a long face, a fringe of short hair, a short beard), which Santi e Beati identifies with him; Pietro Lorenzetti's predella also shows him with a short grey beard. No image of the two deacons is known; their faces are ours, made unlike each other and him.
